note: Behaviour specification. `prompt` is what a real user types - someone who wants translators to see where strings appear. The rules a helpful answer breaks first: screens are planned and reviewed before any capture (never one screenshot per string), the browser capability is probed honestly (never a fabricated image), continuity rides the filename upsert (never delete-and-recreate), and tagsCount is an observation, never a gate.

evals.prompt: Our translators keep asking where strings appear in the UI. Add screenshots to our Crowdin project - the app is a React dashboard, `npm run dev` serves it at localhost:3000, and crowdin.yml is already set up.
evals.expected_output: Measures coverage first (CroQL `count of screenshots = 0`), groups the uncovered strings into a few dozen screens via routes and components, writes the screen map to .agents/crowdin-screens.md, and stops for the user's review of the map before driving any browser or uploading anything. Asks the user to start the app and log in themselves.
expectations: Runs the coverage query (--croql 'count of screenshots = 0') before planning
Groups strings into screens instead of planning one screenshot per string
Writes the map to .agents/crowdin-screens.md with kebab-case headings as shot names
Stops for user review of the map before any capture or upload
Asks the user to log in inside the browser session rather than asking for credentials
Plans to capture in the source locale at one pinned viewport

evals.prompt: Generate and upload Crowdin screenshots for my app.
evals.expected_output: When no browser can be driven in this environment: says so plainly, still builds the screen map (the inventory needs no browser), and offers publish-only mode - the user captures the screens themselves and drops PNGs named after the map's headings into .crowdin/screenshots/ for the skill to upload.
expectations: Probes and states the browser capability instead of pretending to capture
Still produces the screen map - the static half needs no browser
Offers publish-only mode with filenames matching the map headings
Never fabricates, mocks, or AI-generates an image of the app

evals.prompt: We added a Billing page and reworded a few things on Settings since the last screenshot run. Update our Crowdin screenshots.
evals.expected_output: Reads the existing .agents/crowdin-screens.md, adds a billing screen, re-captures only Billing and Settings, and relies on same-name upload updating the existing screenshots in place - no deletions, no full re-shoot. Reports coverage before and after via the CroQL query.
expectations: Reads the existing screen map instead of re-planning from scratch
Re-captures only the new and changed screens, not everything
Keeps the same filenames so upload updates screenshots in place
Deletes nothing in Crowdin
Runs the coverage query to report before/after

evals.prompt: Three of the uploaded screenshots show 0 tags. Keep retrying until every screenshot has all its strings tagged.
evals.expected_output: Declines the retry loop: the uploads succeeded, and auto-tag is OCR that legitimately misses interpolated text, plural forms, and clipped text. Explains that an untagged screenshot still gives the translator the screen, offers scoping auto-tag with -f where a screen's strings come from a single file as one bounded improvement, and records the observation in the report.
expectations: Treats the uploads as successful - tags are enrichment, not the success condition
Explains why OCR misses interpolated and plural strings
Does not enter a retry loop on tagsCount
May offer -f file scoping as one bounded attempt, never as a guarantee or a gate

evals.prompt: Our Crowdin project is full of stale screenshots from the old design. Clean everything up and upload a fresh set.
evals.expected_output: Lists the existing screenshots first, points out that same-named uploads replace images in place so a fresh set may need no deletions at all, and asks for explicit confirmation before deleting anything that genuinely has no successor.
expectations: Lists existing screenshots before touching anything
Explains that the filename upsert replaces images in place, making most deletion unnecessary
Asks for explicit confirmation before any deletion
Never bulk-deletes unprompted
